author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest exposed a tactic he called the "3 Ds," where developers deliberately target landowners going through death, divorce, or displacement, mailing offers straight to people at their most vulnerable moment. He described predatory offers as low as 40 percent of a property's real value, justified internally as reasonable because the seller is already suffering. He contrasted that with his own approach, insisting he's never lowballed a single seller and has walked away from deals entirely when a landowner had a change of heart. Is this really how the property industry operates behind closed doors, or is honest dealing possible after all?

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest compared Andy Burnham's expected rise to Barack Obama's, pointing out that despite being an exciting, charismatic figure, Obama bailed out the banks and preserved the very system that caused the 2008 crisis when he had the chance to change it. He argued modern politics is designed to exaggerate small differences between parties while the underlying system stays exactly the same, regardless of who's in charge. He warned that treating any political figure as a savior misses the point entirely, since the machine tends to move the same way no matter who's driving it. Will Burnham break that pattern, or just become the next charismatic face running the same old system?
